## Introduction

This is a dataset pertaining to gender and compensation at the workplace, modified for ease of analysis and plotting. 

## Data

```{r}
#| label: read-data
#| echo: false
#| message: false

library(tidytuesdayR)
jobs_gender <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2019/2019-03-05/jobs_gender.csv")
glimpse(jobs_gender)
skim(jobs_gender)
```


```{r}
#| label: category-checks
#| echo: false

jobs_gender %>% count(major_category)
jobs_gender %>% gf_histogram_interactive( ~ workers_male)
jobs_gender %>% gf_histogram_interactive(~ workers_female)
jobs_gender %>% gf_histogram_interactive(~ total_earnings_male)
jobs_gender %>% gf_histogram_interactive(~ total_earnings_female)

```

## Download the Modified data


## Plot the Data

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| 

jobs_gender |> 
  filter(year == 2016) |> 
  filter(major_category == "Healthcare Practitioners and Technical") %>%
  ggplot(aes(workers_female / total_workers,
             total_earnings,
             size = total_workers,
             label = occupation)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Salaries and Gender Proportion in the Workforce",
       size = "Total # of workers",
       x = "% of workforce reported as female",
       y = "Total Salary in the occupation (Healthcare") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) 

```
